clue.text: Chaplain said to be employed in Hebridean harbour?

indicators.note: said to be tells us the description that follows is only matched in pronunciation, not in spelling

parts.note: someone guiding boats in a harbour on Skye, an island of the Inner Hebrides, would be a Skye pilot

explanation.surface: A clergyman apparently has a job steering ships into a harbour in the Scottish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is a large island off the west coast of Scotland. The Skye pilot is spoken like the slang term for a padre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is old military slang for a padre, the one who steers souls heavenward.

clue.text: Scottish island saint about to name an Irish county

parts.note: St Kilda is a remote Scottish island group named after a saint
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A holy man from a Scottish island is about to give his name to a county in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to', but 'about' gives RE and 'to name' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the counties of Leinster in the Republic of Ireland, known for horse racing.

clue.text: Not for sale, being invaluable. How very amusing!

definitions.meaning: so precious that no amount of money could buy it
an exclamation at something hilarious, as in 'that look on his face was...'

explanation.definitionFit: Beyond any price means too precious to buy, and colloquially it praises something very funny.

clue.text: In chemist's phial it must act as an indicator

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit within the words chemist's phial it must

explanation.surface: A chemistry vial must contain something that shows acid or alkali.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper treated with a dye that turns red in acid and blue in alkali is a chemical test strip.

clue.text: We are bound to run in this

definitions.text: We are bound to run in this

parts.words: We are bound to run in this
parts.note: 'bound' sounds like 'certain', but two runners have a leg each tied to a partner's

explanation.surface: Someone says it is inevitable that we will compete.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports-day event where partners with adjoining legs tied together hobble to the finish.

clue.text: Caesar's Head valued and put in a case

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so Caesar's Head gives the first letter of that name

parts.note: something valued has been rated or assessed

explanation.surface: A bust of Julius Caesar is appraised and then packed away for shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods packed into a wooden box for transport have been boxed up in this way.

clue.text: "Wild Mustard" — Figaro as inexpert "singer" might do it

parts.words: Figaro as inexpert "singer" might do it
parts.note: Figaro is the barber of Seville; a clumsy singer, one who singes hair, would scorch or char a lock of it

parts.words: Figaro as inexpert "singer" might do it
parts.note: Figaro is the barber of Seville; a clumsy singer, one who singes hair, would scorch or char a lock of it

explanation.surface: A field weed is named, then an opera barber is said to sing badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' in quotes is one who singes, not a vocalist; a barber singeing badly would char a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered weed of cornfields, also called field mustard.

clue.text: Old vessel's engineer invested with order of merit

indicators.note: to be invested with is to be clothed in, so the engineer is wrapped by the other letters
order of means the letters of merit are put in a different sequence

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: An ancient ship's engineer is awarded the Order of Merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order of' turns MERIT into TRIME, which takes RE in the middle; 'order of merit' looks like the honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek galley rowed with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Continental hemisphere of dubious reputation

definitions.meaning: French for half-world, Continental meaning from mainland Europe
describing a fringe class of people, notably kept women, of doubtful standing

explanation.definitionFit: The French term means half-world and names a group on society's fringe with a shady reputation.

clue.text: Statement of grievance I found in factory

indicators.note: found in says the letter is placed within the word for factory

parts.note: a manufacturing plant is a factory

explanation.surface: A worker complains about something they discovered at their workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint or lament, especially a formal one in law, is so called.

clue.text: Make fresh statement concerning a sound partnership

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for concerning or about

indicators.note: sound tells us the words beside it are matched by how they are spoken

parts.note: a partnership is a firm, and with the clue's 'a' before 'sound' the phrase spoken is 'a firm'

explanation.surface: A business statement is reissued about a financially healthy partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it signals that 'a firm' (the clue's 'a' with partnership) is spoken like the verb meaning to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something again is to restate or confirm it once more.

clue.text: Dramatic lady evangelist as an ex-slave in Egypt

parts.note: Mame is the title heroine of the stage musical Mame
Luke is one of the four Gospel writers

explanation.surface: An actress who is also a preacher once lived in bondage on the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mamluks were a soldier caste of former slaves who came to rule medieval Egypt.

clue.text: Old London theatre frequented by Aristotle

definitions.meaning: a historic playhouse off the Strand where Henry Irving acted
the garden in Athens where the philosopher walked and taught

explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by a famous Victorian playhouse in London and the Athenian school where Aristotle lectured.

clue.text: Lacking inclination either way

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone is indifferent, with no preference one way or the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' looks like desire, but here it is slope: something flat has no tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, horizontal surface has no tilt or slope at all.

clue.text: It reduces friction in art club reorganization

indicators.note: reorganization means the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Changes at an art club calm internal disagreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friction' suggests quarrels among club members, but here it is physical rubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil or grease is applied to reduce the rubbing between moving parts.

clue.text: Like the labour of solving the mystery of a Nile death?

definitions.text: Like the labour of solving the mystery of a Nile death?

parts.words: Like the labour of solving the mystery of a Nile death
parts.note: Agatha Christie's Belgian detective Poirot solves Death on the Nile, so his work is named after his first name, while the usual sense is like the mighty labours of Greek legend

explanation.surface: Solving a murder on an Egyptian river cruise is a huge task.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes an enormous task, like those of the Greek strongman, and here also the work of Poirot, whose first name is Hercule.

clue.text: Hardy character, yet a lukewarm type

definitions.meaning: the title figure of Thomas Hardy's novel A ...
someone half-hearted, as the church at Laodicea was rebuked in Revelation for being neither hot nor cold

explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's novel A Laodicean names its heroine after the biblical church scolded for indifference, so the word means a half-hearted person.

clue.text: How cyclist may check for puncture with a laboratory aid

definitions.text: How cyclist may check for puncture
definitions.meaning: a cyclist checks the inner rubber ring of a tyre for a leak
a small glass cylinder used for holding samples in experiments

explanation.definitionFit: Checking a bicycle's inner tube is one sense, and a glass vessel for chemistry samples is the other.

clue.text: Robert's Aurora as winter transport

parts.note: Bob is a short form of Robert, so Robert's is Bob's
Aurora Leigh is a verse novel by Elizabeth Barrett Browning, so Aurora suggests the surname

explanation.surface: A man's possession, named after the dawn goddess, serves as his vehicle in the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: Aurora Leigh is the heroine of Elizabeth Barrett Browning's long poem; Robert was her husband, Robert Browning.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled for racing down an ice track is ridden in the cold season.

clue.text: Invest for starters in best European securities if early growth expected

indicators.note: for starters means take the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.words: best European securities if early growth expected

explanation.surface: Advice to put money first into the best European stocks if early growth is forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' looks like a finance word, but it is the old sense: to lay siege to a town.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town in military terms is to surround it with troops.

clue.text: The power of antidisestablishmentarianism?

parts.note: opposing the disestablishment of the Church of England means being in favour of the C of E, and spelling that support as a preposition plus CE gives a word for power

explanation.surface: A question about how strong the movement to keep the established church is.
explanation.walkthrough: Antidisestablishmentarianism opposed removing the Church of England's official status; CE is the usual abbreviation for Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Power and strength are synonyms, and the clue splits the word into being for the established church.

clue.text: The endless voice, confound it, of the sheep

indicators.note: confound means to mix up, so the letters are jumbled; the exclamation hides the signal
endless means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone curses at the voice of a bleating animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts THE to TH; 'confound it' mixes TH with VOICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy breed of hill sheep named after the hills on the English-Scottish border.

clue.text: Type of hat used in the nursery

definitions.meaning: a close-fitting bell-shaped women's hat popular in the 1920s
a glass or plastic cover protecting young plants in a garden nursery

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for bell names both a bell-shaped hat and a bell-shaped plant cover.

clue.text: Affront offered to the venal Pooh-Bah

definitions.meaning: in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado the corrupt official Pooh-Bah calls the bribes he pockets by this word

explanation.definitionFit: An affront is an offence, and in The Mikado, Pooh-Bah says he must accept each bribe to mortify his family pride, calling it this.

clue.text: Mid cruel distress Coleridge's Abyssinian maid played on it

definitions.text: Coleridge's Abyssinian maid played on it

indicators.note: distress means to torment or knock about, so the letters of the two words are shaken up

explanation.surface: An Ethiopian girl from a poem plays her instrument amid cruel suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's Kubla Khan, 'A damsel with a dulcimer / In a vision once I saw: / It was an Abyssinian maid'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stringed instrument struck with hammers that the girl in Kubla Khan plays.

clue.text: Training ship located so in the region

indicators.note: in says the word for so is set inside the word for the region

parts.note: an area is a region
thus means so, in that manner

explanation.surface: A ship for cadets is moored in this district.
explanation.walkthrough: Arethusa was the name of a famous training ship for boys moored on the Thames, later in the Medway.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known British naval training vessel for boys carried this nymph's name.

clue.text: Believe such titles will be screened

definitions.meaning: to accept as true, to trust
the names of cast and crew shown at the end of a film

explanation.definitionFit: To believe a story is to give it trust, and the lists of film makers rolled on screen are this.

clue.text: Recite arrangement for position of fencing

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters means putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: A performer works out how to recite a piece about swordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing the third of the eight parry positions has this name.

clue.text: Allotted span of the lovelorn Romeo

definitions.text: Allotted span of the lovelorn Romeo

parts.words: Allotted span of the lovelorn Romeo
parts.note: a lifetime is the usual allotted span, but for a lovesick young man parted from his love any wait seems to last for ever

explanation.surface: How long a heartsick young lover has to wait for his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Time without end is how even a short separation feels to someone pining in love.
